text:
infra-alerts-bot: [ALERT] EU standby GPU pool: 15% of nodes failing service role auth, triggering warm-pool thrash and slow joins. Investigating.

maria: seeing lots of `STS:AssumeRole` denies tied to IAM conditional: `aws:SourceIp` - could be a weird NAT churn in the new AZ.
ajay: confirmed — stack traces show sigv4 failures from pv-provisioner: `AccessDenied: Not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRole`.
eren: rolling metric: sustained 200 joins/minute backoff, cost is ticking up due to retries and larger warm pool to keep capacity. tagging this as P1 for capacity ops.
sally: are audit logs showing the exact call context? I only see partial CloudTrail entries — retention window looks normal but there's an ingestion gap into our audit-shipper (zipkin/audit-dataset).
maria: yeah the CT records exist but the audit-shipper failed to POST to collector for ~14m because of an egress rule change in the privatelink subnet. that coincides with the IAM conditional rollout at 02:10 UTC.
ajay: so two simultaneous changes: `iam/conditional-policy-v2` + `egress-fw-tighten-apac->eu` — likely race. we should consider a policy rollback for the IAM change as it's the user-visible auth failure.
ops-runbook-bot: playbook suggestion: 1) revert `iam/conditional-policy-v2` for service-role `gpu-provisioner-role` (canary on 10% of nodes), 2) reopen NAT/privatelink egress for audit shipper, 3) scale down warm pool autoscale target by 20% to reduce cost during mitigation.
eren: +1 to canary first. need to avoid a full rollback that masks a latent infra bug. canary steps:
```
# quick canary rollback
aws iam set-role-policy --role-name gpu-provisioner-role --policy-name conditional-override --policy-document file://conditional-override.json
# conditional-override.json removes SourceIp condition for sts:AssumeRole
```
sally: I'll patch the audit-shipper egress rule to allow collector.fleet.redwood-infra:443 from the privatelink subnet, in case we need logs for forensics.
ajay: deployed the canary override to eu-west-1 (10% of nodes). provisioning error rate dropped from 13% -> 1.5% on the canary pool within 90s.
maria: nice. observe joins latency improved from 1.9s -> 420ms on canary. still see a handful of timeouts from one AZ.
eren: that AZ shows NAT gateway flapping events in the last 20m — weird metric: `natgw.conntrack_exhausted` spikes. could be our ephemeral port usage from audit shipper + warm pool churn.
sally: increasing conntrack_table size is risky for autoscale, but short term we can pin collector traffic to a dedicated ENI and use a static egress path. I'll open a quick route change.
ajay: cost note — if we keep the warm pool inflated while rolling, estimated delta is +$6k/day for EU. ops-runbook-bot: recommendation: enact autoscale stealth mode (reduce desired by 20%) until full rollback or stable for 10m.
maria: agree. I'll leave canary running and start a controlled rollout (25% -> 50% -> 100%) with 5m observation windows.
deploy-bot: deployment started: canary rollback -> 25% at 2026-03-21T14:04:30Z. CI checks green.
eren: we should also add an exception to the IAM conditional that allows `kms:Decrypt` for the `gpu-provisioner-role` when `aws:CalledVia` = `ec2.amazonaws.com` — I saw a KMS decrypt deny in one trace that blocked node bootstrap keys.
ajay: good catch. that KMS deny explains node-level decrypts failing during bootstrap on some instances. adding to rollback doc.
sally: audit shipper egress rule change applied. logs are trickling back in — got the full request context for one failed join: shows `aws:SourceIp` from internal NAT range that wasn't in the allowed list.
maria: final plan: 1) keep canary, 2) expand rollback to 50% now, 3) leave audit egress open, 4) reduce warm pool by 20% to limit cost, 5) follow-up: add IAM exception for KMS decrypt + update conditional to use VPC endpoint id instead of SourceIp.
eren: filing follow-up infra ticket for `vpc-endpoint-based-conditional` and `natgw-conntrack-mitigation`. will include cost impact estimate.
ajay: tagging finance with `@sre-finance` for the $6k/day delta and ask for pre-approval on one-day surge.
maria: thanks team — keeping thread pinned. will update when rollout hits 100%.
deploy-bot: rollout 50% -> success. no new denials in canary slice for 8m.
maria: rollout 100% started. monitoring.
ops-runbook-bot: reminder: once stable, add a short postmortem note to #postmortems with timeline + proposed policy change (use `aws:SourceVpc` or `aws:VpcEndpointId` rather than SourceIp).
